title: A Latent Profile and Network Analysis of Kinesiophobia in Patients After Total Joint Arthroplasty.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Based on the Stress-Multifactorial System, this study aimed to classify heterogeneous subgroups of kinesiophobia in patients following total joint arthroplasty using latent profile analysis, and to identify the key constructs associated with kinesiophobia within each subgroup through network analysis.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: The present study employed a cross-sectional survey design, conducted between April 2025 and July 2026, involving 250 patients after hip or knee arthroplasty at an orthopedic center. Latent profile analysis was performed to identify subgroups of kinesiophobia. Network analysis was conducted to examine the associations among kinesiophobia, pain intensity, pain catastrophizing, rehabilitation self-efficacy, and social support, with the total scores of each scale represented as a node.
RESULTS: In 250 patients after hip or knee arthroplasty, the mean kinesiophobia score was 37.65 ± 4.45, with a prevalence of 48.8%. Two distinct subgroups were identified: the "low kinesiophobia-activity acceptance group" (73.6%) and the "high kinesiophobia-fear avoidance group" (26.4%). Binary logistic regression showed that longer daily pain duration [OR = 2.196,= 0.003], higher Oswestry Disability Index scores [OR = 1.155,=0.002], and negative coping style [OR = 1.322,= 0.013] were associated with greater odds of membership in the high kinesiophobia-fear avoidance group, whereas higher rehabilitation self-efficacy was associated with lower odds of membership in this group[OR = 0.857,< 0.01]. In the "high kinesiophobia-fear avoidance group", pain catastrophizing (PCS) showed the highest centrality (r= 1.424, r= 1.224, r= 1.565). Conversely, in the "low kinesiophobia-activity acceptance group", rehabilitation self-efficacy (SER) showed the highest centrality (= 1.609,= 1.007,= 1.095). Network comparison tests revealed a statistically significant difference in network structure between the two subgroups (= 0.29,= 0.022), but no significant difference in global strength (= 3.27,= 0.078).
CONCLUSION: Patients after total joint arthroplasty display heterogeneous patterns of kinesiophobia across latent profiles, with differences in psychological network structures between subgroups rather than in overall connectivity strength. In the high kinesiophobia-fear avoidance subgroup, pain catastrophizing shows the highest centrality, whereas rehabilitation self-efficacy shows the highest centrality in the low kinesiophobia-activity acceptance subgroup.
